title: HEG Advanced Materials Ltd - 509631 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HEG Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 38% YoY to INR211 crores, margin 29% vs 23%, on better realisation despite marginally lower volumes.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 11% YoY to INR681 crores and standalone PAT rose 53% to INR110 crores, with utilisation above 90%. Management attributed the margin gain to better realisation from product and geographic mix, cost control and efficiency, and said pricing hikes will mostly reach P&L from October onwards as contracts are booked about 3-4 months ahead. Consolidated PAT rose 23% to INR122 crores, and the company remains debt-free with treasury of about INR858 crores. Greentech (TACC anode project, Bhilwara hydro) was detailed in Q&A, and the demerger scheme awaits NCLT order pronouncement.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY from INR154 crores; vs loss of INR126 crores in Q4 FY26
+53% YoY from INR72 crores; vs loss of INR163 crores in Q4 FY26
+17% YoY from INR166 crores; margin 27% vs 25%
+23% YoY from INR100 crores; vs loss of INR119 crores in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR858 crores as of 30 June 2026

segments.name: Graphite electrodes (HEG standalone)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation above 90% in Q1, marginally below last year; realisation gains drove margin expansion. Management said no volumes were lost to the Middle East disruption and utilisation was above 91%.

segments.name: Greentech (TACC anode and Bhilwara Energy)
segments.commentary: Anode project of 20,000 tpa under INR2,200-2,300 crores capex, about 40% spent, targeting commercial production in Q1 FY28 at 40-50% utilisation with INR600-700 crores revenue in year 1. Bhilwara hydro plants (about 300 MW) generate INR320-350 crores FCF a year, debt-free.

guidance_outlook: Management expects prices to rise from October onwards since contracts are booked 3-4 months ahead; bookings are full through September, and October bookings are partly done.
Needle coke cost increase impact expected to reach P&L towards the end of the year (November-January), with a roughly 10-15% rise in total electrode cost cited.
Utilisation expected to close FY27 at 90-95%.
Capacity expansion from 100,000 tpa to 115,000 tpa expected by early 2028.
Management said it expects to maintain Q1 margins (around 28-29% including other income) in coming quarters.
Greentech: anode project EBITDA margin about 35%; by 2030 the company targets a four-digit crore EBITDA across Greentech businesses combined.
TACC debt of about INR1,500 crores expected on a gross basis at 31 March 2027; 70:30 debt-equity funding for the 20,000 tpa anode project.
capex_capacity: Expansion from 80,000 to 100,000 tpa completed; further expansion to 115,000 tpa on track for early 2028 operation.
Anode project (TACC) of 20,000 tpa at INR2,200-2,300 crores capex; about 40% spent so far, with 90% payment targeted in FY27 and balance in Q1 FY28.
Possible 10,000 tpa anode expansion at about INR800 crores capex once the 20,000 tpa unit is complete, with land for about 30,000 tpa; operational by 2029.
Hydro project of 75 MW (acquired from Statkraft, about 30% work done) targeted in about 2.5 years; 300 MW C&I solar project (DC) targeted in about 18 months.
TACC debt secured to date INR1,240 crores from SBI; funding of the 30,000 tpa phase expected 70% debt.
demand_pricing: Middle East represents about 20% of annual sales per management (Q&A); no volumes lost in Q1 per management, with shipping delays absorbed across about 30 countries. Exports are about 70-75% of sales.
US is about 10% of business per management. CVD final result expected end-July and anti-dumping by end-September 2026.
GrafTech and Tokai Carbon announced price increases of USD600-1,200/t and USD930/t respectively, as cited by management; HEG says it will follow suit.
Needle coke prices have risen about USD200-300/t since the Middle East disruption, per management, with impact expected from 3-5 months.
Management cited OECD data of about 71 million tons of new EAF capacity planned for completion by end-2028; estimated 25-30 million tons of EAF capacity commissioned in the last 3-5 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Share of Middle East in revenue, and where were lost volumes diverted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East is about 20% of annual sales. It said no volumes were lost in Q1, with utilisation above 91%, and shipping delays were spread across about 30 countries.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase can be expected in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bookings are 3-4 months ahead, so price hikes start showing from October. New business is at higher prices, and the company plans to follow peers' announced increases.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of other income of about INR43 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Ravi Tripathi said the balance beyond about INR7-8 crores of interest income is fair value gain on investments.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the 30 million tons EAF capacity commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25-30 million tons has come in over the last 3-5 quarters, with the balance over the next 2-3 quarters; projects may slip 10-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Anode project contract coverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Ankur Khaitan said about 70% of the 20,000 tpa capacity will be covered by 3-5 year contracts with Tier 1 players within about 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Debt at Greentech/TACC after the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Om Prakash Ajmera said HEG is debt-free; Puneet Anand said about INR1,500 crores gross debt is expected at TACC by 31 March 2027, with INR1,240 crores already secured from SBI.

qa_highlights.question: Needle coke pass-through timing and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost increase reaches P&L from end-year, and that prices will be raised to cover the rise. CEO said margins in the Q1 range will be maintained and that HEG will earn higher margins than peers.

qa_highlights.question: US exposure and derisking if anti-dumping duties apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US is about 10% of business, that HEG has not dumped in the US, and that volumes can be diverted elsewhere; CEO said HEG will retain the US market.

risks_watch: Outcome of the US CVD (end-July) and anti-dumping (end-September 2026) rulings, with US about 10% of business.
Timing and size of price hikes versus needle coke and energy cost increases; cost pass-through expected only from around November to January.
Middle East conflict affecting shipping, freight, and energy costs, with about 20% of sales from the region.
Demerger scheme: NCLT order pending, record date and timeline not yet announced.
TACC execution: 20,000 tpa anode project, funding (about INR1,500 crores gross debt by March 2027) and commissioning in Q1 FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability and long-term EAF demand, but guarded on pricing specifics and customer or market details, declining to give dollar-per-ton figures or market share. Responses on US trade actions and pricing were deflective and framed around diversification.
key_quotes: We continue to manage these developments through operational efficiencies. Despite all this, the medium- to long-term outlook for graphite electrodes demand remains highly positive.
Stand-alone EBITDA increased by 38% on a year-on-year basis to INR211 crores from INR154 crores, with EBITDA margins also improved to 29% compared with 23% in the corresponding quarter of last year.
So whatever price hikes which will come in, will come in later, will actually start showing up later in the year.
I can only tell you that we'll be able to maintain the margins that we are now talking about.

growth.why: Management expects price hikes to flow into P&L from October (bookings full through September, 3-4 month lag) and needle-coke-driven cost pass-through by Nov-Jan, with utilisation guided at 90-95% for FY27 and 100,000 to 115,000 tpa expansion due early 2028; backing is partly specific (bookings, capacity timing) but the 10-15% electrode cost pass-through and FY28 anode ramp rest on assumptions.
